records.new_gloss_en: extraordinarily impressive or remarkable in degree or quality
records.linguistic_reason: The adjective describes exceptional magnitude or quality, not the philosophical noun phenomenon.

records.new_gloss_en: a soft, sweet fruit with many tiny seeds inside and a thin skin
records.linguistic_reason: Specific edible fruit definition excludes unrelated abbreviation uses of fig.

records.new_gloss_en: an article expressing the opinion of a newspaper or its editors
records.linguistic_reason: Source combines noun editorial and adjective relating to editing; separate grammatical uses need POS scope.

records.new_gloss_en: official permission or approval to proceed with an activity
records.linguistic_reason: Source also includes physical removal and spatial clearance; one approval sense cannot cover all three.

records.new_gloss_en: of the highest quality or most suitable among available choices
records.linguistic_reason: Source also includes adverb '最好地'; the superlative adjective is distinct in grammar.

records.new_gloss_en: a formal agreement between two or more people, groups, or countries
records.linguistic_reason: The noun denotes negotiated mutual commitments; treaty is a governmental subtype.

records.new_gloss_en: an estimate or assessment of how much something is worth
records.linguistic_reason: General evaluation can assess nonmonetary merits; source 评价 may require its own semantic scope.

records.new_gloss_en: a powered flying vehicle with fixed wings that carries people or goods
records.linguistic_reason: The aircraft noun refers to a fixed-wing airplane, not helicopters generally.

records.new_gloss_en: to take part in an activity, or to eat or drink something offered
records.linguistic_reason: Partake in vs partake of have distinct constructions; learner KU needs scope and grammar confirmation.

records.new_gloss_en: a place where people perform their jobs
records.linguistic_reason: The noun refers to a site or environment of employment, not a particular work task.

records.new_gloss_en: welcoming and accommodating people of different backgrounds or needs
records.linguistic_reason: The social inclusion adjective fits original Chinese; numeric 'inclusive of' needs separate context.

records.new_gloss_en: to change information into a particular code or digital form for storage or transmission
records.new_gloss_zh: 编码；把信息转换为代码
records.linguistic_reason: The information-processing verb describes representation, not necessarily encryption.

records.new_gloss_en: a person who is kept prisoner or unable to escape
records.linguistic_reason: The source fits a noun, while captive is also adjectival, requiring explicit POS identity.

records.new_gloss_en: a fault or imperfection that makes something less effective or satisfactory
records.linguistic_reason: The noun fault sense is distinct from the verb defect meaning abandon a country or side.

records.new_gloss_en: a sweet, usually carbonated soft drink
records.linguistic_reason: The original 苏打 may refer to sodium carbonate/bicarbonate or soda water, beyond sweet soft drinks.

records.new_gloss_en: two or more musical notes sounded together to produce harmony
records.linguistic_reason: The second Chinese 弦 can denote a geometric chord or string; musical chord cannot cover those.

records.new_gloss_en: a performance or interview in which someone demonstrates suitability for a role
records.linguistic_reason: The entertainment casting event includes film and stage auditions rather than merely viewing a screen.

records.new_gloss_en: a long narrow part such as a rotating rod or an enclosed vertical passage
records.linguistic_reason: Mechanical shaft and mine/elevator shaft are related by shape but materially distinct referents.

records.new_gloss_en: the act of entering a place by force, especially with an army
records.linguistic_reason: Military or forceful entry supports both core Chinese equivalents, with figurative extensions possible.

records.new_gloss_en: not moving or changing position
records.linguistic_reason: The adjective denotes lack of motion; stationary must not be confused with stationery.

records.new_gloss_en: the ability to bend easily or to adapt to changing circumstances
records.linguistic_reason: Physical pliability and adaptive capacity are conventional extensions, both encompassed by flexibility.

records.new_gloss_en: unkind words or actions that make someone appear foolish or worthy of contempt
records.linguistic_reason: Source may express noun ridicule or the verb 'to ridicule'; POS must be checked before replacing.

records.new_gloss_en: a person who plans and arranges an event or activity
records.linguistic_reason: Person agent sense matches organiser, excluding the physical storage organizer.

records.new_gloss_en: on or to a higher floor of a building
records.linguistic_reason: Source also means adjectival 楼上的, requiring separation from upstairs adverb.

records.new_gloss_en: covered with or full of fine dry particles of dirt
records.linguistic_reason: Literal dust-covered adjective; dusty as a colour is not included.
